name: Fixed platform topsides and substructures
applications: shallow and medium water fixed platforms
principle: Fixed offshore platforms combine a substructure (welded steel jacket, or concrete gravity-base structure) founded on or pinned to the seabed with a topsides deck carrying drilling, production and power. Jackets are launched or lifted in place and piled through legs; topsides are built as integrated or modularised decks and set by float-over or lift. Design is governed by ISO 19902 (steel) and structural reliability against extreme wave, wind and fatigue loads; weight control and deck elevation against air gap are the persistent constraints.

process_steps.name: Jacket fabricated and launched or transported to site
Jacket levelled and pinned with foundation piles
Topsides integrated or modularised, set by lift or float-over

performance.basis: A 14,000 t steel jacket installed in 105 m of water.

source.note: ESDEP lecture notes, offshore structures, read 2026-11-17

limitations: installation weather windows and vessel availability dominate the offshore schedule
decommissioning obligations are engineered in from the start on many regimes
advantages: proven over decades; steel jackets span almost all practical fixed-platform water depths
modular topsides reduce offshore hook-up and commissioning

costs.metric: Heavy-lift crane vessel (SSCV) implied average day rate, Saipem 'best in class' fleet (47 contracts awarded since 2003)
costs.basis: Deutsche Bank modelled implicit day rates from 47 Saipem offshore construction contracts since 2003; modelling assumes installation represents 35% or 45% of reported contract value and OPEX $100k/day for best-in-class assets. Source is an analyst model, not a contracted rate.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Saipem 7000 day rate, current oil & gas contract
costs.basis: Quoted by David Carr (joint CEO, Zero-C) in Breakbulk Magazine as the rate the Saipem 7000 was 'on' in oil and gas, well above wind-sector rates. Vessel one of four able to install 3,000-4,000 t pyramid jackets in >100 m water.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Newbuild semi-submersible crane vessel (SSCV) capital cost
costs.basis: Capital investment stated for a new SSCV with 3-4 year construction time at Samsung/Hyundai/DSME; used to explain why speculative SSCV orders are deterred.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Substation installation vessel day rate, typical
costs.basis: Cost of the substation installation vessel, included in the substation installation contract; 1,000 MW floating wind reference project, 100 m water depth.

costs.metric: Tow-out spread: three anchor-handling vessels (AHVs) combined day rate
costs.basis: Tow-out of assembled floating wind turbine: one primary towing AHV (>=200 t bollard pull) plus two trailing AHVs; included in the floating turbine installation contract.

costs.metric: Large crane vessel time-and-material rate (severance failure exposure)
costs.basis: 'Time and material rates for large crane vessels can exceed $500,000 dollars per day' — used to explain cost exposure if a pile or conductor severance fails and delays the vessel spread.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Sleipnir-class heavy-lift vessel day rate (qualitative only)
costs.basis: Source states only 'Rates for vessels like Sleipnir usually amount to several hundred thousand dollars a day.' No number is published — recorded as a gap, not converted to a figure.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Single-lift topsides installation: overall Phase 1 project cost avoided vs multiple-module lift
costs.unit: NOK (approx USD 124 million as quoted in
costs.basis: Equinor said the single-lift approach trimmed three months off the Johan Sverdrup Phase 1 schedule and reduced overall cost by around NOK1 billion; total Phase 1 project cost quoted as $10.7 billion; single lift also cut ~1 million offshore man-hours.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Topside reception, dismantling and recycling contract value (single-lift removal)
costs.basis: Aker Solutions letter of intent from Allseas for preparatory work, reception, dismantling and recycling of ~50,000 t Statfjord A topside at Stord; excludes the offshore lift by Pioneering Spirit. 'Sizeable' contract = NOK500m-1.5bn by Aker's own definition.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: FPSO marine installation contract value (14 suction anchors, mooring pre-install, tow-out and hook-up)
costs.basis: DOF Subsea Norway contract from Eni Norge, July 2011-December 2013: fabrication and installation of 14 suction anchors, pre-installation of bottom chain, polyester line and buoyancy elements, temporary mooring outside Hammerfest, final tow-out and field hook-up.  Dollar year not stated.

costs.metric: Suction bucket, reference design (92 t, 40 mm wall), fabrication cost
costs.basis: Reference suction bucket with wall thickness 40 mm and weight 92 t; cost benchmark for comparison in EUDP project on industrial-scale suction buckets.  Dollar year not stated.
